numbering: Shared theorem counter: Theorem 1, Corollary 2, Theorem 3, Proposition 4, Lemmas 5–11. Older Lean docstring numbers belong to an earlier manuscript and are not used here.

items.label: Theorem 1
items.title: DFP can fail under strong Wolfe conditions
items.summary: In every dimension n ≥ 2, a uniformly convex C² objective with a globally one-half Hölder Hessian admits a classical DFP sequence satisfying the paper's strong Wolfe parameter range whose gradient norms tend to a positive limit.
items.mapping: Main result, strengthened by the sharpness statement proved later in the paper.

items.label: Corollary 2
items.title: The counterexample can start from the identity
items.summary: An affine coordinate change gives identity initialization, preserves strong Wolfe conditions and one-half Hölder Hessian regularity, and keeps the gradient norms bounded away from zero. The uniform Hessian bounds depend on the coordinate change.
items.mapping: Main result in every dimension n ≥ 2.

items.label: Theorem 3
items.title: A locally Lipschitz Hessian restores planar convergence
items.summary: For a globally strongly convex C² objective in two dimensions, a locally Lipschitz Hessian near the initial sublevel set ensures convergence to the unique minimizer under weak Wolfe conditions, from any positive-definite initial matrix. Strong Wolfe follows as a consequence.
items.mapping: Weak- and strong-Wolfe interfaces; finite stationary termination is represented by constant continuation.

items.label: Proposition 4
items.title: Exact formulas for one DFP step
items.summary: The gradient and inverse-Hessian updates have explicit secant formulas with positive denominators. The matrix update is independent of the line-ratio parameter τ.
items.mapping: Separate declarations prove the gradient formula, matrix formula, parameter independence, and denominator positivity.

items.label: Lemma 5
items.title: Construct a smooth invariant graph
items.summary: A center direction with derivative 1 and contracting stable directions admit a locally forward-invariant smooth graph; invertibility of the stable derivative is not required.
items.mapping: Linked proof components are the metric graph-transform certificate and its finite-smooth regularity interface. These expose supporting hypotheses explicitly; they are not one verbatim Lean statement of the general lemma.

items.label: Lemma 6
items.title: The two-step map has an invariant C⁷ curve
items.summary: The canceled two-step map extends analytically near (0, 2, 1). Its invariant center curve has the stated shape and scale expansions, including ε₊ = ε − (3/2)ε⁴ + (5/4)ε⁵ + O(ε⁶).
items.mapping: Invariant-curve existence, analytic extension, derivative, and signed recurrence are split across declarations.

items.label: Lemma 7
items.title: Control amplitude, angle, and center drift
items.summary: Along the invariant curve, the two-step amplitude, frame angle, center drift, and within-cycle increments have the asymptotic expansions used in the counterexample construction.
items.mapping: Representative proof components for the amplitude and angle estimates and the full-/half-cycle center displacement; see the Lean view for the finer expansion lemmas.

items.label: Lemma 8
items.title: Positive limiting amplitude and a limiting circle
items.summary: The scale is asymptotic to ((9/2)j)⁻¹ᐟ³, the amplitude has a positive limit with first-order tail coefficient 13/3, and the centers converge with cubic tail bounds. The paper identifies the endpoint accumulation set as a circle.
items.mapping: Linked components cover scale, amplitude, and center tails. The circle accumulation-set clause is not represented by this bundle; related topological declarations remain in the full Lean view.

items.label: Lemma 9
items.title: Keep endpoints uniformly separated
items.summary: Every endpoint stays at least a fixed positive multiple of its squared cycle scale away from all other endpoints and the limiting circle.

items.label: Lemma 10
items.title: Interpolate with a C², one-half Hölder correction
items.summary: The disjoint bump correction extends as a C² function across the limiting circle, interpolates the endpoint values and gradients, has a globally one-half Hölder Hessian, and obeys the uniform Hessian bound.
items.mapping: The regularity, interpolation jets, Hölder bound, and Hessian bound are separate declarations.

items.label: Lemma 11
items.title: Nonconvergence forces planar secant degeneration
items.summary: A nonconvergent planar strongly convex secant orbit satisfying weak Wolfe has a positive free coefficient bounded by adjacent-step products and tending to zero. The matrices remain bounded and their smallest eigenvalue tends to zero.
items.mapping: General secant theorem plus the DFP-specialized degeneration interfaces used in the convergence proof.
